name: Hajo (Koch chief)
summary: Father of Hira, so maternal grandfather of Biswa Singha; a chief of Koch Hajo's ancestral line.
notes: Reign not given.

name: Hariya Mandal (Hari Das)
role: Mech chief, father of Biswa Singha
summary: Husband of Hira and father of Biswa Singha; a Mech (Bodo) chief.

name: Sisu (Sisya Singha)
summary: Brother of Biswa Singha, made yuvaraj; his descendants became the Raikut kings of Jalpaiguri.

name: Chilarai (Sukladhwaj)
summary: Third son of Biswa Singha and commander-in-chief under Nara Narayan. Led the 1562–63 invasion that forced the Treaty of Majuli; died of smallpox in 1571.
notes: Spouse: Kamalpriya.

name: Biswa Singha
summary: Son of Hariya Mandal and Hira. Defeated the Baro-Bhuyans and founded the Koch kingdom in Kamata; his sons Nara Narayan and Chilarai followed.
notes: Campaigns began c. 1509; coronation 1515. Sources differ on the cause of death.

name: Nara Narayan
summary: Took the Koch kingdom to its peak with his brother Chilarai as commander. Introduced the Narayani silver coin; Sankardev's teaching spread in his time.
notes: Infobox gives 1554–1587; text gives 1540. Died 1587 (some sources 1588).

name: Lakshmi Narayan
summary: First king of Koch Bihar after the split; submitted to the Mughal subahdar in 1609 and joined the 1612 Mughal attack on Koch Hajo.
notes: Other sources give 1586 for the start and 1627 for his death.

name: Bir Narayan
summary: Pleasure-loving ruler per the Cooch Behar State article.
notes: The district history page gives his death as 1632; another list gives 1627–32.

name: Pran (Prana) Narayan
summary: Reigned almost four decades, one of the longest Koch Bihar reigns before the 18th century.
notes: The district page says he reigned till 1666.

name: Moda (Madan) Narayan
summary: His officers killed Chandra Narayan around 1667; he died in 1680 without a male heir.

name: Basudev Narayan
summary: Killed in 1682 in a skirmish with his kinsman Jagna Narayan.

name: Mahendra Narayan (Koch Bihar)
summary: A minor king, great-grandson of Pran Narayan according to the district page.
notes: Not the Darrang king of the same name.

name: Rup Narayan
summary: Reigned 21 years.

name: Upendra Narayan
summary: Reigned nearly half a century; succeeded by his young son.

name: Devendra Narayan
summary: Installed as a boy under the guardianship of the Nazir Deo, Lalit Narayan; died in August 1765.

name: Dhairjendra (Dhairyendra) Narayan
summary: First reign under the Bhutanese ambassador Pensuthma; deposed in 1770 and abdicated after the 1774 peace between the British and Bhutan, returning in 1775.

name: Rajendra Narayan (1770–1772)
summary: Placed on the throne by Bhutan with Pensuthma as regent.

name: Dharendra Narayan
summary: Two short reigns. After the British captured the capital in 1772 and the 1774 peace with Bhutan, Dhairjendra abdicated in his favour.

name: Bijendra Narayan
summary: Reigned between Dharendra Narayan's two terms.

name: Harendra Narayan
summary: Ruled for over fifty years, under regents until 1801. His reign spans the 1826 end of Ahom rule.

name: Shivendra Narayan
notes: After the 1826 cut-off of the main research; included to complete the Koch Bihar line.

name: Narendra Narayan

name: Jagaddipendra Narayan

name: Man Singha (Koch Hajo prince)
summary: Son of Raghudev and brother of Parikshit Narayan.

name: Raghudev
summary: Son of Chilarai; claimed the eastern Koch lands at Barnagar in 1581 and stopped paying tribute after Nara Narayan died in 1587, making the division permanent. Father of Parikshit Narayan, Man Singha and Mangaldoi (wife of Pratap Singha).
notes: Defeated a Mughal army in 1597. His daughter Mangaldoi married Pratap Singha in 1603.

name: Parikshit Narayan
summary: Eldest son of Raghudev. Defeated by Lakshmi Narayan and the Mughals in 1602 and again in 1612; he surrendered at Pandu in 1614 and was taken to Delhi. His brothers Balinarayan and Gaj Narayan fled to the Ahoms.
notes: Another source gives his death as 1616. The Koch Hajo article lists his reign as 1603–1613 but describes events in 1614.

name: Balinarayan (Dharma Narayan)
relation: Son of Raghudev; brother of Parikshit
summary: Fled to the Ahoms in 1613; Pratap Singha made him tributary king of Darrang (between the Barnadi and Bharali) after the 1615 victory. Fought beside the Ahoms for two decades and was killed at Singri in 1638.
notes: The article's infobox gives 1638 (1639).

name: Mahendra Narayan (Darrang)
summary: Listed as Balinarayan's successor (a son, per some accounts); no dates are given.
notes: Sources conflict on the order of succession.

name: Chandra Narayan (Darrang)
summary: Son of Mahendra Narayan; installed as tributary ruler after Koch princes helped the Ahoms drive out the Mughals.

name: Surya Narayan (Darrang)
summary: Captured by the Mughal commander Mansur Khan in 1682, who installed his five-year-old brother; the Ahoms removed the Mughals later that year.

name: Indra Narayan (Darrang)
summary: A Darrang ruler installed by the Ahoms, listed after Surya Narayan in one genealogy.

name: Hangsanarayan (Darrang)
summary: Executed by royal troops around the time of the Moamoria troubles; father of the rebel prince Krishnanarayan.

name: Krishnanarayan (Darrang)
summary: Rebelled in Darrang in 1791 and occupied North Guwahati with Haradatta; defeated by Captain Welsh in 1792.

name: Chandra Narayan (Bijit Narayan) of Bijni
